text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Monthly inflation for October is expected to top 17 percent and cumulative inflation for the first ten months is seen at 196 percent, the National Statistics Institute said.
-- Bulgaria's state run air companies posted 2,389 billion levs pre-tax profit for the first nine months of 1996, deputy transport minister Svetoslav Stanulov said. @
Financial results of the national carrier Balkan Airways were not included in the calculation, Stanulov said.

- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency has received 18 letters of intent for shortlisting of advisors to the cabinet in the planned sale of 25 percent of the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company, deputy prime minister Doncho Konakchiev said.
-- A European Bank for Reconstruction and Development mission arrived in Sofia to discuss implementaton of a recapitalisation project for the state-owned United Bulgarian Bank. @
-- Bulgaria's state Bulgartabak holding has bought 9,387 tonnes of tobacco from this year's crop from local producers for some 2.3 billion levs, producers said.
-- The state has collected only 34.6 percent of planned annual excise duties in the first nine months, the Finance ministry said.

-- Only 33 out of Bulgaria's 184 military hardware producers are expected to remain state owned under a new strategy blueprint made available to trade union officials by the Industry Minister Lyubomir Dachev. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-84561
